note: The Solana toolchain as DATA. A toolchain bump is an edit to this file and
nothing else: no Kotlin changes, no release. Every component is fetched from
its own upstream (docs/SOLANA.md, 'Where the toolchain comes from'), with
two exceptions we build ourselves: cargo-build-sbf and anchor-cli have no
arm64 Linux binary anywhere, so github.com/cesp99/solana-tools-arm64 builds
them from crates.io on GitHub's arm64 runner, inside the same
debian:stable-slim this manifest installs, with a signed provenance
attestation per archive. Compiling them on the phone instead is still a
manifest edit away (method 'cargo-install'); it costs nine minutes.
Order is the order the Setup screen lists, and the order the guest lane
prefers when more than one row is ready. It is NOT the install order any
more: 'needs' is. The installer runs two lanes at once — one fetches and
unpacks over the network and the host's tar, one runs things inside the
guest — and a row starts the moment every id in its 'needs' is installed
and its own bytes are on disk. Two edges are load-bearing:
* platform-tools needs rustup, because its own postInstall links it into
rustup as the 'thragg' toolchain;
* the two prebuilt drivers need platform-tools (rustup's 'solana'
toolchain, which cargo-build-sbf execs) AND apt (libssl, which both
link) before their verify can run.
estimatedSeconds is what the row took on a Solana Seeker (8 cores, 4 of
them A76) over a home Wi-Fi, measured 2026-09-02 with the timings the
installer logs (`adb logcat -s thragg-toolchain`), from the clean
two-lane run of that day: 12 min 59 s end to end, the gate open at
6 min 40 s (docs/SOLANA.md, 'How long it takes'). For a fetched row the
number is its download plus unpack on the fetch lane. It is the number the
onboarding quotes before a phone has a history of its own, and it is an
estimate, not a promise — the Setup screen says so.
sha256 is over the downloaded file exactly as served. It is also the
component's revision: change the hash and that one row re-installs, while
every other row stays where it is.
releasedNote: Bump this date with every edit. The Update button fetches this same file
adopts it when its date is later than the one in use; the APK's copy wins
back the moment an app update ships a newer one. Keep the two identical:
a bump is an edit here, a copy there, one commit each.
toolsCacheSeedsNote: Every platform-tools tag any installed driver can ask cargo-build-sbf for.
cargo-build-sbf resolves a --tools-version through /root/.cache/solana/<tag>/
platform-tools; a tag with no entry makes it download that release (~450 MB,
1.6 GB unpacked). A symlink to /opt/solana/platform-tools under each tag
makes that a no-op.
The default toolchain is linked as 'thragg', and the name is load-bearing:
cargo-build-sbf 4.2.0 (src/toolchain.rs, link_solana_toolchain) takes the
first rustup toolchain whose NAME CONTAINS 'solana' and, unless it is the
'<rustc>-sbpf-solana-<tag>' entry it wants, UNINSTALLS it. Linked as
'solana' — as it was until 2026-09-02 — the default was deleted by every
build, and the IDL step of the same `anchor build` (which runs on the
default toolchain) died with "override toolchain 'solana' is not
installed". Named 'thragg', it is never looked at; the driver links and
relinks its own '1.95.0-sbpf-solana-<tag>' entries beside it, into the
seeded symlinks, and nothing else moves.
v1.57 — platformToolsVersion, what BuildTasks passes to a Native build;
v1.56 — what cargo-build-sbf 4.2.0 pins when given no --tools-version;
v1.52 — what anchor-cli 1.1.2 passes: its BUILD_SUBCOMMAND constant is
`build-sbf --tools-version v1.52` (src/lib.rs), found on the phone
2026-09-02 as a 5 min 51 s `anchor build` with a failed IDL step.
Seeded twice on purpose: by the drivers' postInstall at setup, and by
BuildTasks.toolchainGuard before every build, for phones set up earlier.
A bump of either driver must revisit this list.

components.name: Debian userland
components.summary: A real Debian under proot. apt works; we maintain none of it.
note: No url and no sha256 here on purpose: this one is the existing
UserlandInstaller/DebianUserland path, which resolves Debian's own
container image through the registry and verifies the registry's digest
as it streams. Duplicating a pinned hash here would pin a tag that moves.
It is also the one archive unpacked THROUGH proot rather than beside it,
because Debian's image carries a hard link (perl) that a host tar cannot
reproduce into app storage — see docs/SOLANA.md, 'Living with proot'.
The proot pass does NOT deliver that hard link either — SELinux denies
link(2) to app processes and --link2symlink's rewrite is host-absolute
on this invocation — so DebianUserland materialises every hard-link
entry as a relative symlink from the tar's own index, and re-checks it
each session.
The verify is not decorative. /bin/sh existing proved nothing when
/usr/bin/perl was silently dropped on a Seeker (2026-08): debconf's perl
frontend exec'd 127, ca-certificates' postinst died, apt exited 100,
days after this component reported success. `perl -e 1` catches that
guest on day one.

components.name: rustup (manager only)
components.summary: The toolchain manager with no toolchain. cargo-build-sbf execs it.
note: --default-toolchain none downloads no rustc at all: platform-tools already
carries one, and a second Rust would be 1.5 GB we do not need. rustup is
here because cargo-build-sbf shells out to it and dies with 'Failed to
execute rustup' otherwise (docs/SOLANA.md).
static.rust-lang.org publishes a .sha256 beside every archived rustup-init;
the hash below is that file's, for 1.29.0/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.

components.name: SBF platform-tools
components.summary: The SBF compiler: its own cargo, rustc and an LLVM with the SBF backend.
note: The load-bearing component. 505 MB down, ~1.4 GB unpacked, and the only
reason a Solana program can be compiled on this device at all.
Unpacked with the host's tar straight into the rootfs — pushing 1.4 GB of
small files through proot's ptrace is many times slower, and this archive
has no hard link to trip over.
postInstall is where rustup is pointed at it. Without the link and the
default, rustup's cargo shim resolves to nothing and every build fails
with a message about a missing toolchain. The link is named 'thragg'
and must not contain the word 'solana' — see toolsCacheSeedsNote.

components.name: rust-analyzer
components.summary: The language server: completion, go-to-definition, the squiggles.
components.note: A gzipped ELF, not a tarball. Ungzipped on this side and chmod 755'd.

components.name: Spettro (agent)
components.summary: The bundled ACP agent. One static binary, no Node anywhere.
note: Unpacked into the same /opt/thragg/agents/<id> layout the agent picker
uses (solana/agents/AgentCatalog.kt, GUEST_INSTALL_ROOT), so an agent
installed by Setup and one installed from the picker are the same thing
in the same place. ACP is behind -acp / --acp; the picker probes it.

components.name: Build tools (apt)
components.summary: gcc, git, pkg-config, OpenSSL headers — what building a program needs.
note: The one step that runs under proot's --link2symlink, because dpkg unpacks
hard links and cannot work without it. Nothing else may use that flag:
under it cargo install hard-links its finished binary out of a scratch
directory it then deletes, reports success, and leaves a dangling symlink
(docs/SOLANA.md, 'Living with proot').
gcc + libc6-dev + make, not build-essential: a Solana program's host
half (build scripts, proc-macros, `cargo test`) needs a C compiler, a
linker and crt files, and nothing here compiles C++ — build-essential's
g++, dpkg-dev and their perl came to ~40 % of what dpkg unpacked.
Sizes are apt's, not ours, so they are estimates and the row says so.

components.name: cargo-build-sbf
components.summary: The build driver. Prebuilt for arm64 by our public GitHub Actions workflow.
note: No arm64 Linux binary of this exists upstream. It used to be built on
the phone (`cargo install`, 2 min 38 s at opt-level 0 after the crate
fetch; 3 min 34 s before) — now github.com/cesp99/solana-tools-arm64
builds it from crates.io on GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runner inside
debian:stable-slim, strips it, and publishes bin/ as this tarball with
a sha256 and a signed provenance attestation (`gh attestation verify`).
Unpacked with the host's tar over /opt/solana/cli, so the marker and
the PATH entry are exactly what the on-device build produced.
postInstall seeds the driver's own tools cache, and it is BUG-1
insurance from the 2026-08 device rehearsal: run without a populated
/root/.cache/solana/<v>/platform-tools, cargo-build-sbf ignores the
1.4 GB toolchain already at /opt/solana/platform-tools and downloads
its own pinned release (~450 MB; the rehearsal's attempt died after
27 min 39 s). A symlink into the cache makes that downloader a no-op.
Three versions are seeded: platformToolsVersion (v1.57 — what
--tools-version asks for; ToolchainManifestTest keeps the two in
agreement), whatever the driver reports as its pin (discovered from
its --version output, which does NOT trigger the download), and v1.56
as the rehearsal-proven pin of 4.2.0 in case that output ever stops
parsing. Duplicates are harmless: ln -sfn is idempotent.
BuildTasks.toolchainGuard repeats the seeding before every build.
postInstall: for v in v1.57 $(/opt/solana/cli/bin/cargo-build-sbf --version 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -n1) v1.56; do mkdir -p /root/.cache/solana/$v && ln -sfn /opt/solana/platform-tools /root/.cache/solana/$v/platform-tools; done

components.name: Anchor
components.summary: The Anchor CLI. It ships no release binaries; ours come from the same workflow.
note: Built by github.com/cesp99/solana-tools-arm64 with `cargo install
anchor-cli --locked` — anchor-cli's own Cargo.lock is the only
combination its releases are tested against. On the phone this was the
long pole: 10 min 26 s, 6 min 23 s at opt-level 0.
Still not required: a Native program builds without it, and the gate
must not be hostage to the largest download in the list.
postInstall seeds the tools cache for v1.52, the platform-tools tag
anchor-cli 1.1.2 hard-codes into every `cargo build-sbf` it runs —
see toolsCacheSeedsNote for what happens without it.
postInstall: for v in v1.52; do mkdir -p /root/.cache/solana/$v && ln -sfn /opt/solana/platform-tools /root/.cache/solana/$v/platform-tools; done
